correctness.rationale: The stationary equations force nonnegative opinion difference; zero difference yields the unique origin. Positive difference forces strictly interior nonzero opinions and leadership, and elimination factors as \((p-q)[a(p+q)-(p^2+pq+q^2)]=0\). The non-symmetric roots satisfy \(\rho=s^2/(a-s)^2\), yielding exactly two same-sign states at every positive ratio and two more unequal polarized states iff \(\rho>16\). The Jacobian splits at the symmetric state with transverse determinant \(\beta a^2\rho^2(\rho-16)/(\rho+8)^2\) and negative trace. At \(a=1,\alpha=1/4,\beta=1/100\), independently regenerated exact quartic polynomials show two same-sign Hurwitz states, a stable symmetric state, and two asymmetric states with a positive real eigenvalue. The embedded exact checker reproduces the matrices and rational Hurwitz signs.

The closest same-author follow-up arXiv:2606.05825 uses a different replicator leadership equation, which is not reducible to the present birth-loss law by a mere parameter change. Analogous pitchfork studies with fixed leaders use different nonlinear interactions. Literature searches and accessible published theorem comparisons returned no equivalent exact theorem; general unpublished reductions remain a novelty risk.

value.rationale: The two-actor mutual-influence network is the natural smallest nontrivial specialization of the motivating 2026 leadership model. The source explicitly leaves its stability boundary undetermined beyond a conservative sufficient bound. A sharp analytically solved parameter boundary together with an exhaustive stationary census and a three-attractor witness distinguishes polarized persistence from same-sign opinion outcomes and supplies a benchmark for the feedback mechanism. This is substantive beyond reparametrizing a known theorem, while no global or empirically accessible-basin claim is smuggled in.
